summary: Round 6 recheck (05:46-06:10 UTC 26 Sep; #37 K2 and #38 twin still PENDING at 06:00Z). Three closed ideas that rounds 1-5 did not re-check, all measured on CPU on the exp60 x138 lab (56 train clips, official metric; base parity FN 1,705 / FP 1,681; post-freeze FP 242 = the round-5 number). (A) STITCH / g=0 end->start re-link (I-164, v3 tracklet-gap 'g=0 idle') STAYS CLOSED. On x138 only 11 of 1,705 FN are both-free end->start breaks (all 6bba; 44b6 0). There are 0 end->start pairs under 7 um, and geometric pairs at 7-15 um are 10 TP / 39 evaluable FP (precision 0.20 against a ~0.48 break-even). Ceiling about +0.0003 lab. (B) EDGE FILTER as a private-only hedge (I-161/I-162; v2 kept it as F2 hedge #3; later closed as 'the in-sample edge-net trap') is PARTLY REVIVED, as a fact plus an OK-gated option. It is not in the plan. The v2 transfer skeptic had shown that exp39's ef gain sits ~90-95% on anomalous transitions (big-step, post-freeze), where drops hit pairs the net never scored (geometric, not in-sample trust). On ordinary transitions a0 predicted -0.0007 and a3 +0.0006, which matches P30 -0.001 and P29 0.000. So probes 29/30 cannot tell 'in-sample trap' apart from 'the public embryo has no freezes'. New x138 measurement, exact official replay: 'efpost' drops final edges with motion_relinked==1, edge_prob==0 and a non-fork source, only on the transition right after a raw frozen frame (np.array_equal). Result: 6bba +0.00174 (SELECTION +0.00265 W/L 7/2, CONFIRMATION +0.00093 W/L 9/3; +0.00093 without the top 2 clips). 44b6 is exactly 0 (no freezes). Pooled +0.00160, dTP -32 / dFP -107 (drop precision 0.77), nodes and divisions unchanged. The unrestricted a0-like drop is sign-unstable (44b6 SEL -0.0039 / CONF +0.0089; 6bba W/L 19/17), which is the P30 pattern again. By construction efpost is a no-op on any freeze-free embryo, so its public read equals K2 unless the public embryo has freezes. R4 therefore cannot validate it; it is a pure private hedge (private = 71%). Expected private gain is about +0.0002..+0.0006 (guess: P(a private embryo has freezes) ~0.5, transfer 0.3-1). Worst case about -0.0005. Decision: only the user can open it, before R8 (27 Sep 12:00 UTC). Default = closed for 29 Sep. (C) LINEFIT-AFTER-HEAD / anisotropic fork-aware RTS smoother (I-184, and the v3 'linefit 0.8->0.6 zero-cost rider') STAYS CLOSED. The x138 base now has the head, and exp60 measured linefit w0.7: 44b6 ALL -0.0031 (SEL -0.0056, CONF +0.0008), 6bba +0.0001 in both halves. Less smoothing on head coordinates does not help. The fork-crossing part is 0.14% of nodes (v2). No plan change; F1 = K2 #37, F2 = twin #38 unless the user takes option B.

findings.what: Edge filter as a private-only finals hedge (I-161 ef_a3_rl_pr, I-162 ef_a0; v2 FINAL_REPORT kept it as idea #3 'F2 carries ef as a private hedge, P(helps private) 0.3'; v2 ef-anomaly-attribution finals policy (b): 'flat P29 -> keep ef in ONE final'). OLD VERDICT: lab +0.0162 CONFIRMATION -> P29 0.947 (tie) and P30 -0.001, read as 'the in-sample edge-network/ILP trap'. The whole EF class was closed (IDEAS.md row 9; RESUME POINT 'CLOSED: edge filter'; memory 'lab over-trusts in-sample ILP/edge net'). WHAT CHANGED: (1) The public LB is one embryo (29%); private is 71% other embryos. (2) Our kernels are deterministic, so P30's -0.001 is a real public step and P29's 0 means |d| < 0.001. Both match the v2 transfer skeptic's ordinary-transition predictions (a0 -0.0007, a3 +0.0006) for an embryo WITHOUT anomalous transitions. So the LB null does not separate 'in-sample trap' from 'public embryo has no freezes or big steps'. On anomalous transitions a0 ~= a3 (drops of pairs the net never scored: geometric, label-free). (3) The base is x138, which has no edge filter, and round 5 showed the post-freeze defect survives on x138 at ~2x normal FN and FP rates (6bba only). (4) R8 still allows a new mechanism until 27 Sep 12:00 UTC, and the runtime headroom covers a freeze scan. NEW MEASUREMENT (exact official replay, 56 clips): 'efpost' drops final edges with motion_relinked==1 AND edge_prob==0 AND source out-degree < 2, only on the transition right after a raw frozen frame (np.array_equal of consecutive volumes). Results: 6bba +0.00174 (SELECTION +0.00265 W/L 7/2; CONFIRMATION +0.00093 W/L 9/3; without the top clip +0.00117, without the top 2 +0.00093); 44b6 exactly 0 (no freezes; no-op by construction); pooled +0.00160; dTP -32 / dFP -107 (drop precision 0.77 vs break-even ~0.52); nodes and divisions unchanged. For comparison: post + big-step (> 3.5 um median final step) pooled +0.00187 (44b6 SEL +0.00044 / CONF +0.00268; 6bba SEL +0.00337 / CONF +0.00061). The unrestricted a0-like drop gives pooled +0.00274 but 44b6 SEL -0.00386 / CONF +0.00894 and 6bba W/L 19/17: ordinary-transition drops are at break-even (44b6 precision 0.51, 6bba 0.57), the P30 failure mode. HONESTY: this is post-hoc and three arms were looked at; 'post' is chosen because its class is defined label-free and exactly, not because it has the best lab number (post_big is higher). NEW VERDICT: PARTLY REVIVED as a FACT (the EF-class closure is over-general: the LB null never tested anomalous transitions). Also a possible OK-gated private-only rider K4 = K2 + efpost. It is not in the plan. Properties: a no-op on freeze-free clips (so public(K4) = public(K2) unless the public embryo has freezes); no network trust; nodes unchanged. Risks: the lab detector and head are in-sample on train clips; freeze prevalence in the hidden embryos is unknown (the train embryos are 1 of 2 with freezes; 6bba 30/39 lab clips); R4 cannot read it on public; round 5 rejected post-freeze FIXES (re-link) for 29 Sep on the same grounds. Guessed EV: private +0.0002..+0.0006, worst case about -0.0005.

findings.what: For lab arithmetic, the official edge FP rule: a predicted edge is evaluable (can be FP) iff its SOURCE is matched to a GT node with out-degree > 0 OR its TARGET is matched to a GT node with in-degree > 0 (not 'both endpoints matched'). With a 'both matched' rule, FP is undercounted ~20x (6bba normal transitions: 20 vs 1,135 FP). Any quick CPU estimate must use this rule; with it, my matcher reproduces the lab's FN 1,705 and FP 1,681.
